heroHeadline: Trump 'More Seriously Thinking' of Restarting Combat in Iran — Ceasefire on Life Support; New Sanctions Imposed; Kuwait Reports IRGC Port Attacks — Day 74
heroSubtitle: Day 74 (May 12): A CNN source confirmed Trump is 'more seriously thinking of restarting combat operations in Iran' as diplomatic deadlock deepened following Tehran's and Washington's mutual rejection of each other's proposals. Iran declared it is 'ready for any aggression' with its 'finger on the trigger.' The US imposed new sanctions targeting Iranian nuclear research and 12 Chinese/Iranian entities supporting Iran's ballistic missile program and oil sales. Kuwait reported IRGC drone and missile attacks on Shuwaikh Port and Mubarak Al Kabeer Port — one Kuwaiti soldier injured, four IRGC operatives detained; the UAE condemned the incidents. An Iranian MP publicly floated the threat of 90% uranium enrichment if US attacks resume — widely seen as a pressure tactic. The Iraqi supertanker Agios Fanourios I, which had cleared the Strait of Hormuz, turned back near the US naval blockade before reaching Vietnam. Pentagon acting comptroller confirmed the war has cost at least $29 billion; Hegseth and Gen. Caine testified on Capitol Hill. Trump departs for China on May 13 — no major decision expected before that trip. Day 73 (May 11): Iran-US negotiations in full deadlock; Brent surged to ~$103.93/bbl; Iran warned Europe against deploying warships to Hormuz; ~1,550 ships with ~22,500 sailors stranded in the Persian Gulf.
